spec.title: PROP-070: Validated resource addresses and selected resolution

p.RESOURCE-SCHEME-LAW: The strict resource vocabulary has two disjoint schemes. A classified native Vibe document uses `spec://<group>/<name>[@<exact-version>]/<logical-doc-path>[#<anchor>[.<child>…]]`; a named ordinary CommonMark source export uses `resource://<group>/<name>[@<exact-version>]/<export-name>`. `group/name` is a validated qualified package coordinate, never an undotted host token or wildcard. An exact selected dependency has the selected version in its canonical spelling; the self coordinate is unversioned. No query, percent-encoded alternative spelling, empty authority/path/anchor component, dot traversal, backslash or control/whitespace spelling is admitted by this value grammar. Parsing never treats an authored string as a filesystem grant.

p.SELECTED-RESOURCE-AUTHORITY: A dependency address is constructed only against a finite selected `(group,name) → (version,root)` world. An omitted version means that selected version, not the semver-newest directory; an explicit exact version must equal the selected one. A package absent from the selected world, a malformed version, a wrong selected version and an invalid qualified coordinate have distinct refusals. The root's self coordinate names its authored Vibe tree and cannot carry an `@version`. A caller without selected-world evidence cannot publish a canonical dependency resource by scanning installed slots. A lock selection identifies the intended package but does not itself prove a readable file, safe physical containment or valid source bytes.

p.VIBE-DOCUMENT-ADDRESS: A strict `spec://` resource points only to a source classified as a Vibe document. Its logical path is relative to that source's selected specs root, extensionless and independent of Markdown/XML serialization (PROP-045 `ADDRESSING-UNCHANGED`). `PROP-NNN` and `FEAT-NNN` descriptive physical stems canonically cite their abbreviated ID only when the existing exact prefix lookup has one match; two matching slugs, a Markdown/XML pair or competing active forms refuse instead of taking the first directory entry. The optional dotted anchor is an ordered path of the current ASCII fact/heading ID segments; absence denotes the whole document. This address layer validates spelling and selected document identity; actual anchor existence, uniqueness, byte observation and caller-specific errors remain the owning read path, not a fabricated successful document.

p.SOURCE-EXPORT-ADDRESS: A `resource://` path is exactly the package-unique `[[package.source_exports]].name` validated by PROP-072 `SOURCE-EXPORT-SELECTOR`, never a raw package-relative file path or Vibe anchor. Constructing it requires the selected package identity and the matching row in that package's parsed metadata at the selected version; a free-standing validated row cannot claim membership in another package. The declaration selects one file and a root-to-section heading-title path, but it grants no physical read, source interpretation or trust. Before content is returned, the source descriptor must select ordinary CommonMark with matching media and the caller must capture/recheck bytes and reject missing or ambiguous sibling headings. A `resource://` export cannot be converted to a `spec://` Vibe fact by suffix, marker text or successful parsing.

p.UNSUPPORTED-RESOURCE-REVISION: Legacy `SpecAddress` may parse `~rN`, but strict resource construction refuses every revision pin as `unsupported_revision` until a revision-aware captured source owner exists. It never drops the pin or serves the live document while claiming the requested revision. A malformed `~` spelling is a grammar refusal, distinct from a well-formed unsupported revision.

compatibility.title: 2. Explicit legacy conversion and refusal corpus

p.LEGACY-RESOURCE-CONVERSION: The existing `SpecAddress` parser and legacy `FileResolver` remain for incumbent compiler/boot callers during migration; they are not a public resource fallback. A new strict value is made only by explicit conversion with the exact selected-world resolver. Qualified legacy `spec://` documents may convert when their version, logical path and unique resolved stem can be proved; an omitted dependency version is filled from selection. An undotted host authority, nonselected package, guessed newest-installed slot, unsupported revision, foreign physical serialization path or ambiguous abbreviated stem never silently converts. A legacy `@=version` spelling may convert only if it equals selection; canonical output omits the `=`. A source export is constructed from its separate validated row, never guessed from a legacy Vibe citation.

p.RESOURCE-REFUSAL-CORPUS: Corpus cases classify accepted canonical Vibe and export spellings, unique abbreviated stems and explicit selected versions, plus typed refusals for percent encoding, empty segments, malformed/foreign versions, missing selection, wrong selected version, duplicate ID stems, two physical forms of one Vibe document, undotted host and supported-syntax-but-unavailable revision. No first-match directory order, suffix-based resource interpretation, lexical path normalization or unreadable-as-not-found claim is introduced by this address slice. Portable physical containment and source-read failure propagation belong to the later A.2/A.3 owners.

p.PORTABLE-SOURCE-COMPONENTS: Before traversing a selected directory for a document, each authored relative path component and active serialization suffix obeys the existing `vibe-safefs` portable component law. The resolver preserves exact logical spelling; it never normalizes a drive, UNC, alternate-data-stream, device, trailing-dot, control or dot-segment spelling into an apparently valid source. At every traversed child and final file, a different spelling with the same shared NFC/full-case-fold physical identity is a typed alias refusal, even on a host whose native filesystem would distinguish the two. A selected Vibe descriptor row uses that same relative component and identity law rather than a local lowercase/character blacklist. A no-follow preflight refuses symlinked children before any selected source path is returned. This is a portable read-side lookup rule, not an OS race-free captured read or a claim of native Windows/macOS qualification; physical byte capture and complete read-error propagation belong to later owners.

p.INTERNAL-LOOKUP-FAILURES: Compiler-facing section sources, recursive `#embed` reads and selected-provider prompt resolution preserve the incumbent selected-world authority and portable source preflight. An actually absent document is `not found`; an existing non-directory source location or failed directory operation is unreadable; duplicate physical document stems, competing pattern members and a referenced duplicate document anchor refuse as ambiguous instead of selecting the first or disappearing from a set. A matched pattern member missing its document alone is excluded from that set. If a selected source disappears after lookup, the caller reports instability; if its subsequent held observation cannot be established, the caller reports unavailable and never publishes partial bytes as stable content. These internal checks preserve valid Markdown/XML projection and prompt/embed content. The portable lookup preflight alone is not a read grant; the production reader uses the separate retained observation law below, whose finite window does not exclude later namespace races. The public captured query owner remains separate.

p.PREPARED-VISIBLE-SOURCE-AUTHORITY: A query receives one opaque prepared authority for the selected node, never free lock rows or an ambient dependency-directory scan. The constructor consumes the node's exact authored identity/root, the already ordered selected resolution, the owner visibility verdict and caller-supplied captured source bytes plus descriptor identities. The node is its own self authority; admitted dependencies come only from that node's effective visible closure at their selected versions and materialised roots. A hidden, unselected, newest-but-not-selected or wrong-owner package cannot become readable by the presence of a slot. Parsed declarations, a package content hash, a descriptor row and a portable physical preflight are distinct from captured bytes and never manufacture them. Missing prepared capture returns unavailable. Construction performs no provider fetch, hydration, cache fill or current-source read; the separate preparation owner must supply captures. This initial world binding does not by itself prove later membership continuity or a retained-handle query read, which belong to the following owners.

p.SELECTED-WORLD-CONTINUITY: A prepared point query retains the exact selected resolution and the authored membership chain from the workspace root to its selected node. The preparation owner supplies bounded snapshots of the governing lock and those membership manifests; the query constructor does not fetch or rebuild them. Before captured bytes can be used, current no-follow observations must agree with the retained selected lock rows, selected-node membership, selected source manifests, descriptor identities and captured outputs. A changed selected lock or descriptor refuses as stale; missing or unreadable required evidence makes the selected world unavailable. Only the selected node's ancestor chain, retained dependency metadata required to establish its visibility, and effective visible source outputs are inspected: an unrelated broken workspace member or unselected slot cannot veto a proven point query. Observation is detection-bound, not an atomic filesystem transaction or a claim that source names cannot change after the final check; a query never combines prepared old-world bytes with a newly observed source.

p.RETAINED-SOURCE-OBSERVATION: A source read that returns bytes and a raw SHA-256 digest obtains both from one bounded, no-follow SafeFS observation under a held project root, parent and regular single-link file. The same observed buffer supplies any parsing or projection input; a separately reopened name cannot supply the digest or the parser's bytes. The read checks the held file across two passes and the final capability-relative name before reporting a stable observation. Absence before opening remains absent; an unreadable, shared-link or unstable observation never returns partial bytes as success. This is a finite pre/post stability window: mutation after the final check, including hostile ABA, is not excluded by this witness. A query read creates no lock, directory, copy-on-write output, cache fill or provider effect. Native platform qualification is separate from portable source-code behavior.

p.CAPTURED-SOURCE-MEMBERSHIP: A source-proven result requires a bounded complete capture of the original package tree, replayed with the existing named content-hash recipe and checked against the independently selected source hash and exact package pin in the current prepared world. Only after that comparison may an immutable path-to-captured-bytes index grant original-file membership. The supported bounded recipe-zero replay has explicit count, size and depth limits; an unsupported recipe or incomplete capture remains unavailable offline rather than falling back to a new local hash or fetching the package. A document absent from the verified original index cannot become source-proven because an installed slot contains it.

p.SOURCE-STRENGTH-LAW: An observed result states only that the held source bytes were read. Record-consistent states that selected slot-record rows, source mapping and materialized output bytes agree locally. Source-proven additionally establishes that the returned original source bytes are a member of the independently verified original capture under the selected package hash. Record-only, payload-only and coordinated record-plus-payload changes cannot promote local agreement to source proof. A development or in-place source without independent captured package proof remains observed. A transformed output can carry proof of its original source member but remains at most record-consistent as returned output until a separate converter/overlay derivation is proved; the source and output strengths are never conflated. Strict requests for absent required capture or unsupported recipe refuse without provider, cache or rebuild effects.

derivation.title: 8. Builtin derivation and materialized semantic location

p.BUILTIN-DERIVATION-PROOF: Derivation-proven materialized bytes require the opaque source-proven capture minted by the canonical original-tree replay, an authored Vibe source descriptor selecting those exact original bytes, the named current builtin converter recipe, an authorized package adoption overlay whose independently observed identity agrees with the selected slot record, and that record's exact source-to-output row. The converter runs purely in memory over captured bytes, applies the authorized overlay, and its emitted bytes must equal the held materialized output byte-for-byte before the derived strength is returned. A caller-supplied output digest, raw catalogue, editable record or output file cannot mint this proof. Converter, overlay, mapping or output drift refuses. A native/custom converter has no implicit execution path and remains unavailable until separately proved.

p.CANONICAL-NODE-LOCATION: The logical document stem and anchor are source-neutral. A separately versioned hash of the canonical SpecDoc IR node has the same value for semantically equivalent Markdown and XML materializations; it is distinct from original-source SHA-256, materialized-output SHA-256 and specmap's existing source-span `content_hash`, whose meaning is never silently changed. A materialized locator is resolved from the actual selected output bytes and carries that output's real extension and native line range. Whole-slot `Mixed` is a materialization policy, not a document parser: copied or Mixed Vibe outputs retain the selected source descriptor's media, while converted outputs use the named converter's target media. The selected interpretation opens the matching Spec or Doc vocabulary, including Doc-only blocks, before native positions are returned. Original-source file/line and raw hash cannot be published as an installed-output locator or as evidence of cross-form semantic drift. A new wire representation versions its schema rather than reinterpreting any e1 field.

extraction.title: 9. Classified captured extraction and shared node selection

p.CLASSIFIED-SOURCE-EXTRACTION: A prepared source query consumes the selected authored descriptor and held captured bytes before choosing a parser. Only declared VibeSpec or VibeDoc opens the matching SpecDoc vocabulary; CommonMark exports use the ordinary CommonMark reader and preserve literal Vibe-looking annotations. XmlData and opaque resources retain their exact bytes and cannot mint Vibe fact facets. An unavailable optional structured view does not hide raw content. Same-stem ordinary resources are distinct selected rows, not competing Vibe serializations. No extraction fetches, rebuilds or promotes a local digest to original-source proof.

p.SHARED-SPECDOC-SELECTION: One shared SpecDoc IR selector serves selected read_spec content and the compiler's exact #embed selection. It selects a whole document, an exact section subtree, or one addressed fact carrier in a paragraph, list item, table cell or other position permitted by the selected vocabulary. Authored documentation pNN anchors use their retained IR identity rather than inventing facts in ordinary prose. A dotted path follows the actual anchored ancestry. Unknown and ambiguous paths refuse with candidates; no nearby node or whole-document fallback replaces the requested node. With children=false a section returns only its own heading, status and direct blocks; nested sections are excluded. Outline and per-node canonical representation byte sizes and heading chains are derived from the captured IR without a prebuilt specmap.

p.SELECTION-REPRESENTATION-BASIS: Every extracted result identifies selected descriptor/manifest and capture identities, media/interpretation, encoding, representation recipe and exact span basis. A raw span refers only to exact captured bytes; an emitted IR fragment or XML-to-Markdown projection carries its own explicit representation basis and never pretends its positions are raw source coordinates. Original-source, materialized-output and canonical semantic hashes retain their existing distinct strengths. Selection and optional inspection have explicit bounded resource limits and truthful unavailable outcomes.

p.TABLE-FACT-INDEX: Canonical specmap extraction inventories each permitted table-cell fact and permitted quote facts in the same document anchor namespace as paragraph/list facts. Header positions confer facts only where the selected dictionary permits them; ordinary table header structure does not itself mint a fact. Equivalent Markdown and XML td carriers expose the same addressed facts and explain reachability. A literal inline-code marker, an ordinary resource or a foreign dictionary position cannot mint a fact. Source/projection index positions and actual selected-output locations remain distinct.

p.GENERATED-SOURCE-QUERY-CONTRACT: The epoch-one source query request, result and refusal are registered generated contracts. CLI spec read and MCP read_spec call one read-only selected-source service; spec_resolve uses the same address/observation owner. ServerContext supplies the host project root, never an argument root, provider or effect bridge. Preparation and query are distinct: the host prepares bounded selected membership, lock, descriptor and held output observations through incumbent owners; an unavailable prepared world refuses without fetching, hydrating or rebuilding. Strict selected read_doc composition uses this same source resolver while retaining its documented whole-page, projection and translation behavior. Legacy standalone four-source documentation composition remains explicit, never an implicit strict fallback.

p.SOURCE-QUERY-OBSERVATION-BINDING: The owning service validates success and refusal, including epoch and closed input fields, before a surface renders them. Expected resolution, selected source and captured document hashes and continuation cursors bind one measured observation and exact request selection/format; stale data never mixes with old bytes. A cursor bounds exact UTF-8 content chunks of that selected representation, never widens a node to a whole-document fallback. Unknown package/document/anchor and ambiguity return typed bounded candidates. The returned canonical address, dictionary/status, heading chain, selected/full representation sizes and proof strength preserve their distinct roles.

p.SOURCE-QUERY-NATIVE-LOCATION: A source-neutral document/anchor locator is resolved against actual retained selected output bytes at query time. Results name the real materialized slot extension, native line range and explicit native encoding/span basis, separately from emitted content recipe and chunk offsets. An unavailable or ambiguous range, stale observation, failed copied-unconverted structured representation or unsupported transform refuses instead of publishing original-source or projection coordinates as a slot location. No query gains lifecycle effects from machine discovery descriptors or optional server effect hosts.

p.SOURCE-QUERY-DOC-COMPATIBILITY: Explicit schema=1 read_doc validates its closed generated address/format/language request before preparation and uses the same selected captured resolver as read_spec. Its existing whole-page projection ignores the anchor, numbers documentation blocks and may select an admitted language adaptation or fall back to the captured source language. It never falls back to an in-tree package, store or newest slot when strict capture is unavailable. The generated reply separates the returned page projection recipe/byte size from selected input observation and native location; input coordinates and hashes do not describe the expanded page bytes. No-schema read_doc preserves standalone four-source compatibility with an explicit legacy-four-source authority label. Original-source or derivation-proven strength is never inferred from this projection. PROP-045's Doc Markdown projection is intentionally one-way: strict semantic Doc reading requires retained compatible XML pivot bytes. A converted Markdown-only Doc returns explicit structured unavailable while its exact raw captured bytes remain retrievable; no Example/Prompt nodes are guessed from prose and no original capture is fetched or rebuilt.

p.SOURCE-QUERY-CURSOR-CORRELATION: A continuation binds the exact request, representation and captured source object through the existing SafeFS same-host observation correlation token. Object replacement with equal bytes cannot reuse an old cursor when the observed identity differs. Correlation is finite and non-authoritative: operating-system identity reuse or hostile ABA can defeat this observation window, and a token is not portable across hosts or an authenticated source proof.
